segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After this Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias, and he revealed himself in this way.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Simon Peter, Thomas who was called the Twin, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Simon Peter said to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I’m going fishing.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We are coming with you too.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They went out and got into the boat, and that night they caught nothing.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When dawn was already breaking, Jesus stood on the shore; the disciples, however, did not know that it was Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Children, you don’t have any fish, do you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “No.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they cast it, and they were no longer able to haul it in because of the great number of fish.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So that disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “It is the Lord!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he tied his outer garment around him, for he was stripped for work, and threw himself into the sea.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the other disciples came in the boat, dragging the net full of fish, for they were not far from land, only about two hundred cubits away.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they got out onto the land, they saw a charcoal fire laid there, with fish lying on it, and bread.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Bring some of the fish you have just caught.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Simon Peter went aboard and hauled the net to land, full of large fish, a hundred and fifty-three of them; and although there were so many, the net was not torn.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Come, have breakfast.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: None of the disciples dared to ask him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Who are you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for they knew it was the Lord.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and likewise the fish.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This was now the third time that Jesus was revealed to the disciples after being raised from the dead.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they had eaten breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Simon son of John, do you love me more than these?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Feed my lambs.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to him again, a second time,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Simon son of John, do you love me?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Shepherd my sheep.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to him the third time,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Simon son of John, do you love me?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter was grieved that he said to him the third time,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do you love me?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and he said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Feed my sheep.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, when you were younger, you used to fasten your own belt and walk wherever you wanted; but when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will fasten your belt and carry you where you do not want to go.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said this to indicate by what kind of death Peter would glorify God. And after saying this, he said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Follow me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following, the one who had also leaned back against his chest at the supper and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, who is the one handing you over?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So when Peter saw him, he said to Jesus,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, and what about this man?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So this saying went out among the brothers and sisters, that that disciple would not die. Yet Jesus did not say to him that he would not die, but,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This is the disciple who is testifying about these things and who wrote these things, and we know that his testimony is true.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But there are also many other things that Jesus did; if every one of them were written down, I suppose that not even the world itself would have room for the books that would be written.

notes.note: This is the lake more often called the Sea of Galilee. The name comes from the city of Tiberias on its western shore, founded by Herod Antipas and named for the emperor Tiberius.

The Greek word can mean completely unclothed, but in ordinary usage it also described someone wearing only an undergarment or loincloth, as a labourer would. Most scholars think Peter was lightly clad for fishing and tucked or tied on his outer garment before going to meet Jesus. Some hold instead that he was wearing only a smock, which he belted up in order to swim.
A cubit was the length of a forearm, roughly 45 centimetres or 18 inches. Two hundred cubits is about ninety metres, or a hundred yards.

This word occurs in only one other place in the New Testament: the charcoal fire in the high priest's courtyard where Peter stood when he denied Jesus three times (John 18:18). Many interpreters think the echo is deliberate, setting the scene for the threefold question that follows.

notes.traditional: an hundred and fifty and three
notes.note: Since antiquity readers have proposed symbolic meanings for this number, but no explanation has won general agreement. It may simply be an eyewitness detail, since fishermen counted a catch in order to divide it.

The Greek can mean 'more than these other disciples love me', 'more than you love these men', or 'more than you love these things', meaning the boat and nets. Most interpreters take the first sense, recalling Peter's earlier claim to outdo the others in loyalty. The translation leaves the phrase as open as the Greek does.

Jesus' first two questions use the verb agapaō and his third uses phileō, while Peter answers with phileō each time. An older and still popular reading sees a contrast between a higher love and mere affection. Most current scholars judge the change to be stylistic, since this Gospel uses the two verbs interchangeably elsewhere, and the passage also varies its words for 'know', 'feed' and 'sheep' without a clear difference in meaning. Both verbs are therefore rendered 'love'.

The next verse says that this saying points to the manner of Peter's death. Ancient writers used the stretching out of the hands as an expression for crucifixion, and early Christian tradition held that Peter was crucified in Rome. Most interpreters read the phrase in that light, though the image taken by itself could describe a helpless old man being dressed and led.

The verb means to hand over or deliver up. It is the ordinary word for delivering someone into custody, and it does not by itself carry the sense of treachery that 'betray' does. The traditional rendering is 'betray', which fits what Judas did but adds a colouring the Greek word leaves to the context.
The Greek plural, traditionally 'brothers' or 'brethren', was the normal way to refer to a mixed group of siblings. Here it means the community of believers, women as well as men.

The shift to 'we' and then to 'I' in the next verse has led most scholars to conclude that these closing lines, and perhaps the whole chapter, were added by members of the beloved disciple's circle, who vouch for his testimony. Others take the 'we' as the author's own manner of speaking. No surviving manuscript of the Gospel lacks this chapter.

candidates.reason: Used across the Gospels of Judas and of the authorities; 'betray' versus 'hand over' changes the tone, and readers would notice inconsistency between chapters.
The plural for the believing community recurs throughout Acts and the letters, and translators divide between 'brothers', 'brothers and sisters' and 'believers'.
The single and doubled 'amen' formula on Jesus' lips recurs throughout the Gospels and needs one fixed English form.
Whether to distinguish it in English from ἀγαπάω should be decided once for John and the rest of the New Testament.
It recurs in John, Paul and 1 John, where 'reveal', 'show', 'manifest' and 'appear' are all in use and a reader would be misled by variation.
